record.paper_title: Several Open Problems in Operator Theory
record.context_brief: Spectra of restriction to algebraic subspace
record.original_question: Let X be a complex Banach space, let T in L(X) be a bounded operator, define the point spectrum pi(T) = {lambda in C : lambda - T is not injective}, and define the surjective spectrum pi_prime(T) = {lambda in C : lambda - T is not surjective}. Let Y = E_X(T) be the linear subspace obtained as the union of p(T)^{-1}(0) over all nonzero polynomials p, equivalently the sum over lambda in C of generalized kernels (lambda - T)^{-infinity}(0). Let T_Y : Y -> Y be the restriction of T to Y. Are pi(T), pi(T_Y), and pi_prime(T_Y) equal?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a complex Banach space and $T \in L(X)$ a bounded linear operator. Define:
- the point spectrum $\pi(T) = \{\lambda \in \mathbb{C} : \lambda - T \text{ is not injective}\}$;
- the surjective spectrum $\pi'(T) = \{\lambda \in \mathbb{C} : \lambda - T \text{ is not surjective}\}$.

For each $\lambda \in \mathbb{C}$, let $(\lambda - T)^{-\infty}(0) = \bigcup_{n \ge 1} \ker((\lambda - T)^n)$ denote the generalized kernel at $\lambda$. Define the algebraic subspace
$$Y = E_X(T) := \bigcup_{\substack{p \in \mathbb{C}[z] \\ p \ne 0}} \ker p(T) = \sum_{\lambda \in \mathbb{C}} (\lambda - T)^{-\infty}(0),$$
which is a (not necessarily closed) $T$-invariant linear subspace of $X$. Let $T_Y : Y \to Y$ denote the restriction of $T$ to $Y$, viewed as a linear operator on the vector space $Y$.

Question: Is it true that
$$\pi(T) = \pi(T_Y) = \pi'(T_Y)?$$
